summary: Revises the FTP reply codes, updating RFC 542. Reply codes are the numeric responses a file transfer server sends to indicate success, failure or progress.

eli5.summary: When a computer asks another to move a file, the answer comes as a number meaning yes, no or wait. This updates which numbers mean what.

what is a multi-line ftp reply
subtitle: A new scheme of three-digit FTP reply codes where the first digit alone tells a program whether a command worked.

tldr.problem: FTP user processes needed an easy way to tell the outcome of each command without reading the reply text, and some had trouble watching the command and data connections at once.
tldr.mechanism: Each reply is a three-digit code plus text. The first digit says good, bad or incomplete, the second groups the kind of reply, and the third refines it. Multi-line replies are bracketed by the same code, and the preliminary reply to a transfer command now comes before the data connection is established.
tldr.outcome: The code is for programs and the text is for people. The result modifies the protocol of RFC 542, and the two together specify the FTP implementation at socket 21.

today: RFC 640 updates RFC 542, and the unit metadata shows no RFC that obsoletes or updates it. Its status is listed as Unknown.

sections.title: Purpose of the Revision
sections.content:
RFC 640 describes a revised set of reply codes for the File Transfer Protocol. The aim is for a user protocol interpreter to determine whether a command succeeded or failed by examining the first digit of the reply code.

It also changes command sequencing. Earlier, when a transfer command (STOR, RETR, APPE, LIST, NLIST, MLFL) was issued, the preliminary reply was sent after the data connection was established, which troubled interpreters that found it hard to monitor two connections asynchronously. Now the preliminary reply says the file can be transferred and that the connection either already exists or is about to be attempted.

The revision modifies the protocol of RFC 542; the implementation at socket 21 (decimal) is the protocol specified by the two together.
sections.eli5: The helper now says 'okay, starting' before the delivery truck is ready, so the program only has to watch one thing at a time.

sections.title: Reply Format and Multi-Line Replies
sections.content:
A reply is a three-digit number, sent as three alphanumeric characters, followed by text. The number is for automata that decide what state to enter next. The text is for the human user and may differ from server to server, so the user-process need not examine it.

Formally a reply is the code, a space, one line of text and the TELNET end-of-line code. For longer text, the first line starts with the code followed by a hyphen, and the last line starts with the same code followed by a space. The user-process just looks for the second occurrence of that code and a space at the start of a line. A middle line that starts with a 3-digit number must be padded by the server to avoid confusion. Multi-line replies are not nested, and system messages carry no reply codes.
sections.eli5: A long answer starts and ends with the same number, like opening and closing quote marks, so the reader knows where it stops.

sections.title: What the Three Digits Mean
sections.content:
The first digit gives the verdict: 1yz positive preliminary (expect another reply before the next command), 2yz positive completion, 3yz positive intermediate (more information needed, used in command groups such as USER, PASS, ACCT), 4yz transient negative completion (the action did not happen but may be requested again) and 5yz permanent negative completion (do not repeat the exact request).

The second digit groups the topic: x0z syntax, x1z information, x2z connections, x3z authentication and accounting, x4z unspecified, x5z file system. The third digit is the finest detail. A rule of thumb for 4yz versus 5yz is whether the command can be repeated unchanged and still succeed.
sections.eli5: The first number is like a traffic light: go, done, need more, try later, or stop. The next two numbers say what the trouble is about.

sections.title: The Defined Reply Codes
sections.content:
The RFC lists the codes in groups. Examples include 200 Command okay, 500 Syntax error, command unrecognized, 502 Command not implemented, 220 Service ready for new user, 230 User logged on, 331 User name okay, need password, 150 File status okay; about to open data connection, 226 Closing data connection; requested file action successful and 550 Requested action not taken: file unavailable.

The reply text is only suggestive, but the codes should be followed strictly: servers should not invent new codes for slightly different situations, and new ones are to be proposed to the FTP committee through Jon Postel. The restart marker reply 110 has exact text, MARK yyyy = mmmm. A command that is irrelevant at a site, such as ALLO at a TENEX site, gets 202 so a simple user-process can carry on. The RFC ends with a command-by-command list of possible replies.
sections.eli5: There is a list of numbers, each with a meaning like 'okay', 'not found' or 'password please', and everyone agrees to use the same numbers.

viz.caption: FIRST DIGIT OF AN FTP REPLY (RFC 640)

items.label: Positive Preliminary
items.desc: Action is being initiated; expect another reply.

items.label: Positive Completion
items.desc: Action completed; a new request may start.

items.label: Positive Intermediate
items.desc: Command accepted; more information is needed.

items.label: Transient Negative
items.desc: Action did not happen, but it may be requested again.

items.label: Permanent Negative
items.desc: Action did not happen; do not repeat the exact request.

references.text: File Transfer Protocol, RFC 542, whose protocol this RFC modifies.
